prompt: What does Azure do with the image named in a new machine's imageReference?
hint: The machine has a disk of its own from the first boot.

choices.text: Boots the machine directly from the image, which is shared by every machine made from it
choices.why: That is the file picture. Nothing boots from an image; every machine gets its own disk.

choices.text: Copies it into a new managed disk, and the machine boots from that copy
choices.why: The image stays where it was and can be copied again for the next machine.

choices.text: Downloads it to the machine's temporary disk and installs it
choices.why: Nothing is installed from an image; its blocks become the OS disk.

choices.text: Moves the image into the machine's resource group
choices.why: The image is not moved or consumed; the next machine can use it too.

prompt: A team asks for Trusted Launch on a machine whose size is in the Dv3 series. What stands in the way?
hint: Trusted Launch protects one generation of machine.

choices.text: Trusted Launch is priced extra on the older series of sizes
choices.why: Microsoft's documentation says Trusted Launch adds nothing to the price.

choices.text: Trusted Launch is offered only for Windows machines
choices.why: Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL and others are on the supported list.

choices.text: The Marketplace image has to be a managed image first
choices.why: It is the other way round: managed images are what Trusted Launch does not support.

choices.text: That series cannot run generation 2 at all
choices.why: Dv3 is among the sizes the documentation lists as unable to run generation 2, and Trusted Launch protects only generation 2.

prompt: A generation 2 machine starts from UEFI firmware; a generation 1 machine starts from ___.
hint: The older firmware of a PC.

prompt: The same Ubuntu machine is created once with az vm create and once from a Bicep file using API version 2024-07-01 with no securityProfile. How do the two compare?
hint: The defaults belong to the tool and to the API version.

choices.text: Both get Trusted Launch, because Ubuntu supports it
choices.why: Support is a condition, not a default. At 2024-07-01 a missing securityProfile gives Standard.

choices.text: Both are Standard, because Trusted Launch is never a default
choices.why: The CLI and the portal default to it, and so does API version 2025-11-01.

choices.text: The CLI's has Trusted Launch and the template's is Standard
choices.why: Two boots from one intention, and nothing fails to say so: which is why the course writes the security type down.

choices.text: The template's deployment fails until securityProfile is added
choices.why: It succeeds, with a Standard machine. The omission is silent.

prompt: Which of these are recorded by an image and decide whether a creation succeeds? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three were in this section.

choices.text: The generation it was built for
choices.why: A generation 1 image does not boot as generation 2.

choices.text: The processor architecture, x64 or Arm64
choices.why: An Arm64 size needs an Arm64 image.

choices.text: The security types it supports
choices.why: Trusted Launch needs a generation 2 image that supports it.

choices.text: The region's price for the size
choices.why: A price belongs to the size and region, not to the image.

choices.text: The name of the machine's resource group
choices.why: Any resource group can hold a machine made from any image.

prompt: Match each part of Canonical:ubuntu-24_04-lts:server:latest to what it names.
hint: Publisher, offer, SKU, version, in that order.

pairs.right: The organisation that publishes the image
The newest build, chosen at creation

right_distractors: The region the image is stored in

prompt: az vm image list printed two warnings and a table without Ubuntu 24.04. What does the table show?
hint: Read the first warning to its end.

choices.text: The CLI's own built-in copy, used because the download failed
choices.why: Sixteen popular images frozen into CLI 2.91.0. The fetched document has Ubuntu2404.

choices.text: Every image Azure offers in brazilsouth today, newest build first
choices.why: That needs --all, and --all needs a subscription.

choices.text: The images this subscription has accepted the licence terms of
choices.why: There is no subscription here, and terms are a separate command.

choices.text: Images Canonical has withdrawn
choices.why: The list is popular images, not retired ones.

prompt: A colleague writes image: 'Ubuntu2404' into a Bicep file's imageReference. What is wrong?
hint: Ask who translates an alias.

choices.text: Nothing, if the CLI that deploys it has fetched the alias document
choices.why: The CLI translates aliases for its own --image; a template goes to Resource Manager as written.

choices.text: The alias needs a version after it
choices.why: An alias already stands for a URN with latest; the problem is where it is used.

choices.text: The alias belongs to the CLI, and Azure itself has never heard of it
choices.why: imageReference takes the four names, or an id. Aliases exist only inside the CLI.

choices.text: Ubuntu2404 points at a generation 1 image
choices.why: It points at server, which is generation 2.

prompt: Two machines are created from Canonical:ubuntu-24_04-lts:server:latest, in March and in April, from an unchanged template. What can you say about their OS disks?
hint: latest is answered at a moment.

choices.text: They are identical, because the template did not change
choices.why: The template names a question, not a build.

choices.text: The April machine fails, because latest was resolved in March
choices.why: Nothing is resolved in advance; each creation asks again.

choices.text: The compiler fixed the build number when the file was compiled in March
choices.why: The compiled template still says latest, as the transcript showed.

choices.text: Each was copied from the build that was latest on its own day
choices.why: latest is a question asked at creation. The template says nothing about which build.

prompt: vm.bicep compiled with securityType: 'TrustedLaunh' and no warning. What does that show?
hint: Lesson 1 said what a warning is. This is the other half.

choices.text: The compiler corrected the spelling silently when it wrote the template
choices.why: The template carries TrustedLaunh, as jq showed.

choices.text: To the compiler it is a plain string, so any value passes
choices.why: No warning is not proof of a right value; only what the types make strict is checked.

choices.text: Azure accepts any spelling of a security type
choices.why: Nothing on the laptop can say what Azure accepts; the request decides.

choices.text: Trusted Launch is turned off once the file compiles
choices.why: Compiling turns nothing on or off; it writes a template.

prompt: Put the steps of capturing a generalised Linux image of your own in order.
hint: The machine is cleaned from inside before Azure is told.
items: Create a machine from a Marketplace image and configure it
Deallocate it with az vm deallocate
Mark it with az vm generalize
Capture it as a gallery image version
trap: Marking it generalised before deprovisioning leaves a machine that cannot start again with its old user and keys still inside.

prompt: Why is a gallery image version preferred over a managed image for the shop's machines?
hint: Three limits of the managed image were named.

choices.text: A managed image cannot hold Ubuntu
choices.why: It can hold any generalised Linux machine.

choices.text: A managed image is deleted once its first machine has been created from it
choices.why: It can create many machines; it is reused like any image.

choices.text: It stays in one region and subscription, with no Trusted Launch
choices.why: Those are the documented limits; the gallery has none of them.

choices.text: A gallery version needs no generalised source
choices.why: True, but it is not why: the shop's image is generalised either way.

prompt: Ten machines are created from a specialised image of shop-build. What do they have in common that a generalised image would have avoided?
hint: Specialised means nothing was cleaned.

choices.text: The same computer name and the same accounts as shop-build
choices.why: A specialised image is a copy of the original, accounts and name included.

choices.text: A slower first boot than a generalised image
choices.why: The other way round: specialised boots faster, having been set up once.

choices.text: A new osProfile each, from the template
choices.why: A specialised image has no osProfile; there is nothing to set up.

choices.text: No SSH keys at all
choices.why: They keep the original's keys, which is the problem.

prompt: A package in cloud-init.yaml fails to install on a new machine. What does Azure report about the machine's creation?
hint: cloud-init does not wait for your configuration.

choices.text: It fails, and the machine is deleted
choices.why: A failure inside custom data is not a provisioning failure.

choices.text: It succeeds, and the machine looks healthy
choices.why: Which is why the documentation tells you to build your own way of hearing about it.

choices.text: It waits until the package installs, up to forty minutes
choices.why: That limit belongs to the Linux Agent running a script; cloud-init reports ready without waiting.

choices.text: It retries the whole creation from the image
choices.why: Nothing is retried; first boot happens once.

prompt: When does loadFileAsBase64('cloud-init.yaml') read the file?
hint: Look at what jq found in the template.

choices.text: When the machine first boots
choices.why: At first boot cloud-init reads custom data that is already in the request.

choices.text: When Resource Manager receives the deployment from the CLI
choices.why: Resource Manager never sees your laptop's files.

choices.text: Every time the machine restarts and cloud-init runs again
choices.why: Custom data is for first boot, and cannot be changed on a single machine.

choices.text: When bicep build runs, which writes it into the template
choices.why: The compiler wrote it in as a variable; a change to the file reaches Azure only through the next compile.

prompt: A definition holds 1.2.0, 1.9.4 and 1.10.0, and 1.10.0 was published with excludeFromLatest. Which version does a machine naming only the definition get?
hint: Compare as numbers, then remove the excluded.

choices.text: 1.10.0, because it is the highest number
choices.why: It is the highest, and it is excluded from latest.

choices.text: 1.2.0, the first one published
choices.why: latest is not the oldest, and order of publishing does not count.
The highest number that is not excluded. 1.10.0 is still usable by its own id.

choices.text: None: the deployment fails while a version is excluded
choices.why: Exclusion only removes one candidate.

prompt: A scale set will create 120 machines at the same moment from one image version in brazilsouth. Following the documentation's rule of one replica per twenty machines created concurrently, how many replicas should brazilsouth keep?
hint: Divide by twenty.

prompt: An image version's OS disk is 64 GB and holds 12 GB. It is replicated to two regions with three replicas in each. How many GB of snapshots are billed?
hint: Each replica is a snapshot of the occupied size.

prompt: A definition was created with hyperVGeneration V1, but the shop's machines are generation 2. What is the fix?
hint: The documentation lists what a definition lets you change.

choices.text: A new V2 definition
choices.why: A definition declared with the wrong generation is replaced, not edited.

choices.text: Edit the definition's hyperVGeneration to V2
choices.why: Generation is fixed at creation; it is not on the list of changes.

choices.text: Publish the next version with hyperVGeneration V2
choices.why: A version cannot have a different generation from its definition.

choices.text: Set excludeFromLatest on every version
choices.why: That changes which version is latest, not what kind of image they are.

prompt: The shop's finance team, in another subscription of the same tenant, needs to create machines from shop-web. Which sharing fits?
hint: Pick the narrowest that reaches them.

choices.text: A community gallery, so that anyone can find it
choices.why: That publishes the images to every Azure customer.

choices.text: Copying the image into a managed image in their subscription
choices.why: A managed image cannot be shared across subscriptions at all.

choices.text: Nothing: a gallery is visible to every subscription in its tenant from the start
choices.why: A gallery is private to its subscription until shared.

choices.text: An RBAC role on the gallery for their group, plus the image's id
choices.why: RBAC reaches people and groups in other subscriptions; they cannot list the image, so they need its id.

prompt: gallery.bicep compiled with osState: 'Generalised' refused and hyperVGeneration: 'v2' accepted. Why the difference?
hint: Both were typed by hand; only one is strict in Microsoft's types.

choices.text: One is a closed list; one is free text
choices.why: A warning catches what the types make strict, and nothing more.

choices.text: The compiler checks the spelling of a value but never its upper or lower case
choices.why: It refused a spelling and passed a case, but because of the types, not a rule about letters.

choices.text: v2 is a valid generation and Generalised is not
choices.why: The compiler did not decide that; it could not check v2 at all.

choices.text: API version 2024-03-03 does not support generation 2
choices.why: It does: V2 is one of its values.

prompt: Put the gallery's resources in order, from the outermost to what a machine's disk is copied from.
hint: One holds definitions; a definition holds versions.
trap: A machine is never created from the definition; it is created from a version, and the copy is read from one of its replicas.

prompt: The shop wants every new web machine to start with Docker installed, and each to know its own order-API version. How should that be split?
hint: Bake what is slow and rare to change; configure what differs per machine.

choices.text: Both in custom data, so no image is needed
choices.why: That works, at the price of an install on every creation and a dependency on package mirrors.

choices.text: The runtime in the image, the setting at first boot
choices.why: Slow and rare to change goes in the image; what differs per machine goes in custom data.

choices.text: Both baked into a gallery version, one version per API version
choices.why: That makes a new image for what is only a setting.

choices.text: Both in a specialised image of one configured machine
choices.why: Every copy would share its name and accounts, and still carry one version.

prompt: A version is replicated to brazilsouth with 3 replicas and southcentralus with 1. Its image holds 10 GB. How many GB of snapshots are billed?
hint: Count the replicas; outbound data is a separate charge.
